clue.text: Attachment to one sound tree in coastal strip

parts.note: an attachment or tie is a bond
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: sound tells us the tree's name is heard, not spelt, so we enter the shoreline word it resembles

parts.note: the beech is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone looking for a strip of land where a tree that makes a noise is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' makes BEECH heard as BEACH. Bondi Beach is the famous surfing beach in Sydney.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondi Beach is a well-known stretch of Australian shoreline, an example of a coastal strip.

clue.text: Last of flour in roll to be consumed

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the bread roll

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of flour

explanation.surface: A baker's final bit of flour in a roll that is about to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn is to be consumed by fire.

clue.text: Sick aunt to recover without medicine

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters of aunt are unwell and out of order

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: An ill relative getting better without drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering naturally means by the body's own processes, without medicine.

clue.text: Composer's gravity risks no upset

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of gravity risks no are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A composer's serious demeanour is not endangered by being disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Mrs Simpson turns up, inspiring good piece of wit

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the reversed name takes the next piece inside
turns up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Marge is Mrs Simpson in the TV cartoon The Simpsons
pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: Mrs Simpson arrives and prompts a witty remark.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGE reversed is EGRAM. Mrs Simpson suggests Wallis Simpson; it is the cartoon mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, clever saying, a piece of wit.

clue.text: Missionary's short newspaper piece, book, and article

indicators.note: short means the newspaper piece loses its last letter

parts.note: a column is a regular newspaper piece
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A missionary's brief newspaper piece, a book and an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Columba was the Irish missionary who brought Christianity to Scotland from Iona.

clue.text: Take water back holding one?

indicators.note: holding means the reversed word wraps round the next piece
back says the word for drinking like a cat is read from right to left

parts.note: to lap is to take water with the tongue
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An instruction to return some water while carrying a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: LAP reversed is PAL, and 'holding' puts I inside it. The whole clue also describes a bucket, which holds water.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket is a vessel that takes water and holds it, the job the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Wimbledon champion's name: Grey

parts.note: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1975

explanation.surface: A tennis champion's name is Grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale grey, the colour of ash.

clue.text: The French Resistance about to break the levees-they may be swallowed

parts.note: la is French for the
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: to break means the short word splits the embankments open from inside

parts.note: dykes are embankments holding back water, like levees
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: French Resistance fighters about to breach the flood banks, which may be overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' signals the container. Lardy cakes are rich sweet breads made with lard, an English regional speciality; 'swallowed' suggests flood water, but means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardy cakes are sweet buns that people eat, so they are things that may be swallowed.

clue.text: How amiably competent priest starts meal?

definitions.meaning: doing something cheerfully and without resentment
a priest skilled at blessings opens dinner by saying a fine blessing

explanation.surface: A capable priest opens dinner in a friendly manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a grace is a prayer said before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something willingly and pleasantly is doing it amiably.

clue.text: Almost covered ground again in nostalgic style

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: to cover ground again on foot is to have retrod it

explanation.surface: Someone nearly walked the same path a second time, in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes styles that deliberately imitate the past, which is nostalgic fashion.

clue.text: Maybe I curse that woman, after Gilbert's private has misplaced wife

indicators.note: after places the pronoun at the end, behind the soldier's name
misplaced means a letter is shifted to a different spot in the soldier's name

parts.note: Private Willis is the sentry in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta Iolanthe
that woman is her

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether to swear at a woman who came after a misplaced wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has misplaced' shifts the wife's letter to the end of the soldier's name. The definition is an example: if I curse someone, I wish them harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who curses another wishes them ill, so the speaker cursing is an example of a malevolent person.

clue.text: Novel shows remarkable artistry, including both text and writing style

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters wrap round the next pieces
remarkable suggests the letters of artistry are worked into something new

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a text
a person's hand is their style of handwriting

explanation.surface: A novel praised for its artistry in both content and prose style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges the fodder to TRISTRAY, and 'including' wraps it round the two abbreviations. 'both' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is the eighteenth-century comic novel by Laurence Sterne.

clue.text: Study cafe and its cooking to take away

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of cafe and its are being mixed up

explanation.surface: Examining a cafe and its food in order to seize them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two words of fodder; 'take away' tempts as a takeaway meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to seize property officially, taking it away.

clue.text: Large container of matured spirit I broke into

indicators.note: broke into means the letter forces its way inside the word for matured

parts.note: something matured is old
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A big container of aged liquor that the speaker broke open.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large steel barrel, a kind of big container.

clue.text: Imposing article, is Lady Bracknell

parts.note: august means imposing or majestic
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A statement that an imposing article is a famous stage character.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Bracknell, the formidable aunt in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, has the first name Augusta.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is Lady Bracknell's first name in Oscar Wilde's comedy, so the name identifies her.

clue.text: Religion of peace fascinated by ideology

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet, so it stands for peace
to be into something is to be fascinated by it
an ism is an ideology

explanation.surface: A faith of peace that is captivated by a doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shintoism is the indigenous religion of Japan.

clue.text: Pay quick visit from the States for bridge?

definitions.text: Pay quick visit from the States
definitions.meaning: to ... is to cross the Atlantic for a brief visit
a road bridge carrying one road over another

explanation.surface: Someone making a brief trip from America to see a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a flyover is a road bridge over another road; in the US the word means a flypast, but here the US is only where the visitor flies from.
explanation.definitionFit: A road carried over a junction on an elevated structure is called a bridge, a sense of the British word.

clue.text: Evidence of vermin in part closing wings of alert hospital

indicators.note: closing means the actor's part shuts round the next pieces

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

indicators.note: wings of asks for the outer letters of alert

explanation.surface: Signs of rodents found in a section next to a watchful hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole gnawed by rodents is a sign that vermin are present.

clue.text: Simple table, a bit short — cheat!

indicators.note: a bit short means the final letter of the times table is lopped off

parts.note: the two times table is the simplest multiplication table

explanation.surface: Someone told off for cheating at an easy multiplication table that ends too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO TIMES (table) loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to cheat on a partner by seeing someone else.

clue.text: Set for work, lugged computer equipment across lake

indicators.note: across means the verb spans the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: took means carried, as lugged does
IT, information technology, covers computer equipment

explanation.surface: Someone hauled computer kit across a lake for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolkit is a set of tools for doing a job of work.

clue.text: Change of mind in moment, but extremely tactless

parts.note: a second is a moment
though can mean but

indicators.note: extremely asks for the end letters, the extremes, of the word tactless

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind in an instant after being very blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsidering a decision is having later reflections on it, a change of mind.

clue.text: Accurately detect break in voice

definitions.meaning: to perceive or spot something, as in noticing an error
a sudden crack in someone's voice, from emotion

explanation.definitionFit: A catch in the voice is a brief break caused by emotion; to catch also means to detect.

clue.text: Nick -—- opener's out for duck

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and it is out, removed

parts.note: to nick is to steal

explanation.surface: A batsman is out for a duck, nicking the ball first up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is a first batsman, and a duck is a score of nought; here the opener is the first letter and the duck is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: Without this in tank, I conk out?

definitions.text: Without this in tank, I conk out?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of tank, I and conk are disordered

explanation.surface: A motorist fears the engine will stop without an additive in the tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TANKICONK; the whole clue explains what an antiknock additive is for.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiknock agent is a fuel additive stopping engine knocking, without which the motor may conk out.

clue.text: Assistant received head of section secretly

indicators.note: received means the assistant takes the letter inside

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of section

explanation.surface: A helper quietly took delivery of the head of a department.
explanation.definitionFit: Words said as an aside are said privately, so the term can mean secretly.

clue.text: Genuine article returned — counterfeit initially accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the reversed word takes the initial inside it
returned means the article is read backwards

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of counterfeit

explanation.surface: A real item sent back after a fake was at first taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning authentic or genuine.

clue.text: Gather mole is struggling from the earth's heat

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of gather mole writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: A mole battling to collect warmth from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Geothermal describes energy derived from the heat inside the earth.
